411.explanation: In the tenth pauri of Japji Sahib Guru Nanak lists what deep listening to the Name brings, starting with truth, contentment and spiritual wisdom.
411.tie_back: The Kural calls the wealth gained through the ear the foremost of all wealth; Japji says the highest treasures, truth, contentment and wisdom, come through listening.
411.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 3, Japji Sahib (pauri 10), Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
411._accuracy_note: Reasonable fit: the Suniai pauris make listening the source of spiritual riches, but the listening meant is to the Name and the Guru's word, not to learned people in general.

412.quote_or_event: “Upon this Plate, three things have been placed: Truth, Contentment and Contemplation. The Ambrosial Nectar of the Naam, the Name of our Lord and Master, has been placed upon it as well; it is the Support of all.”
412.explanation: In the Mundavani at the close of the Granth, Guru Arjan describes the scripture as a plate of spiritual food: truth, contentment, contemplation and the Name.
412.tie_back: The Kural ranks food for the ear above food for the stomach; Guru Arjan also offers truth, contemplation and the Name as the food that truly sustains.
412.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1429, Mundavani, Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
412._accuracy_note: Reasonable but partial: both treat wisdom as nourishment, but the Mundavani does not rank it against bodily food or tell anyone to eat less.

413.explanation: In the ninth pauri of Japji Sahib Guru Nanak says that by listening, ordinary people rise to the standing of the highest beings, here named as Shiva, Brahma and Indra.
413.tie_back: The Kural says those rich in hearing equal the gods on earth; Japji likewise says listening raises a person to the rank of the gods.
413.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 2, Japji Sahib (pauri 9), Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
413._accuracy_note: A strong fit on listening raising people to the rank of gods, though for the Guru the deities are lesser beings within God's order, not objects of worship.

414.explanation: In the eleventh pauri of Japji Sahib Guru Nanak says that listening lets even those without sight, read by commentators as the spiritually ignorant, find their way.
414.tie_back: The Kural tells the unlettered to listen anyway, since hearing will be their support in hardship; Japji promises that listening guides even the blind.
414.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 3, Japji Sahib (pauri 11), Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
414._accuracy_note: A strong fit: both make listening open to those without other resources; Japji speaks of finding the path rather than of support in misfortune.

415.quote_or_event: “I am blind; Your Name, O Creator Lord, is my only anchor and support.”
415.explanation: In Raag Tilang Bhagat Namdev calls God's Name the support of a blind man; the Gurmukhi word tek is glossed by Sahib Singh as a walking stick.
415.tie_back: The Kural calls the words of the upright a staff for one walking on slippery ground; Namdev calls the Name the walking stick of the blind.
415.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 727, Raag Tilang, Bhagat Namdev (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
415._accuracy_note: Next-best only: the walking-stick image matches, but Namdev's support is God's Name, not the counsel of virtuous people.

416.quote_or_event: “Within the mind are gems, jewels and rubies, if you listen to the Guru's Teachings, even once.”
416.explanation: In the sixth pauri of Japji Sahib Guru Nanak says that hearing even one teaching of the Guru fills the mind with treasures.
416.tie_back: The Kural says to listen to good things, however little, since even a little brings full greatness; Guru Nanak says even a single teaching heard yields jewels.
416.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 2, Japji Sahib (pauri 6), Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
416._accuracy_note: Near match on how much even a little good hearing yields; the teaching meant is specifically the Guru's.

417.quote_or_event: “Listening-dive deep into the ocean of virtue.”
417.explanation: In the eleventh pauri of Japji Sahib Guru Nanak says that listening lets a person explore the depths of virtue; Sahib Singh glosses it as gaining insight into endless virtues.
417.tie_back: The Kural says those who have examined things finely and gathered much learning by hearing will not speak foolishly; Japji says listening gives a deep understanding of virtue.
417.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 3, Japji Sahib (pauri 11), Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
417._accuracy_note: Next-best only: it shares the idea of depth gained through listening, but says nothing about guarding against foolish speech after a mistake.

418.quote_or_event: “O my ears, you were created only to hear the Truth.”
418.explanation: In Anand Sahib Guru Amar Das tells his ears that their purpose is to hear the Truth and the Name.
418.tie_back: The Kural says ears not opened by instruction are as good as deaf; Guru Amar Das says ears exist to hear the Truth, so ears that do not are failing their purpose.
418.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 922, Raag Raamkalee, Anand Sahib (pauri 37), Guru Amar Das (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
418._accuracy_note: Near match on the true purpose of the ear; the Truth meant is God's Name, not instruction in general.

419.quote_or_event: “Sweetness and humility, O Nanak, are the essence of virtue and goodness.”
419.explanation: In Asa di Vaar Guru Nanak names sweetness and humility, not size or show, as the heart of every virtue.
419.tie_back: The Kural says only those refined by careful listening can speak humbly; Guru Nanak makes humble, sweet speech and bearing the essence of goodness.
419.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 470, Raag Aasaa (Asa di Vaar, salok), Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
419._accuracy_note: Reasonable fit on humble speech as a mark of worth, but Guru Nanak does not trace humility to listening.

420.quote_or_event: “O Baba, the pleasures of other foods are false. Eating them, the body is ruined, and wickedness and corruption enter into the mind.”
420.explanation: In Siree Raag Guru Nanak contrasts the true food of the Name with other foods, whose enjoyment harms the body and fills the mind with corruption.
420.tie_back: The Kural scorns beast-like people who know only the tastes of the mouth and not those of the ear; Guru Nanak likewise rejects the palate's pleasures in favour of spiritual nourishment.
420.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 16, Siree Raag, Guru Nanak (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
420._accuracy_note: Reasonable fit on rejecting the palate's pleasures for higher nourishment, but the shabad is about the Name, not hearing, and it has no beast image.
